answer: A registration ratchet on join velocity: before attesting, each new agent burns a hash chain whose length depends on how many identities arrived the previous day. One arrival pays nothing; the ten-thousandth in a day pays orders of magnitude more. Bulk registration becomes a purchase of compute, since anyone can forge a keypair cheaply and nobody can forge the electricity behind ten thousand of them. The curve moves like a glacier, symmetric in both directions, so a sybil burst cannot wait out a relaxation. Honest operators joining alone never notice. The table is fixed as onyx in each client.
